correctness.rationale: For each wheel, the anchored polar inequalities are exactly the spoke and rim inequalities. Cyclic Fubini gives the trace of a self-adjoint Hilbert-Schmidt operator. Even/odd eigen-equations reduce to the complete two arithmetic spectral progressions; their signed trace powers give all polar volumes. A convergent cotangent identity gives the generating function. A published primal-volume theorem and dominance of the unique largest eigenvalue yield the Mahler asymptotic. Independent Ehrhart-difference enumeration in exact integer arithmetic agrees for m=3..8; no finite enumeration is used as the proof for all m.

Another general result characterizes polar lattice points via matroid cuts without specializing the corresponding volume. Independent mathematical-record comparisons concern wheel facets, inradii or Löwner ellipsoids, not dual continuous volumes or the exact exponential Mahler rate. The original wheel polar spectral trace is not a corollary of the published primal formula alone; residual unindexed transfer-operator literature risk remains.

value.rationale: Mahler volume is a central affine invariant of finite-dimensional Banach unit balls. The natural wheel sequence previously had an exact primal volume but no evaluated dual factor in inspected literature. Completing the product in all dimensions, obtaining a closed generating function, and deriving a quantitative exponential separation from the Hanner benchmark (growth base strictly above 1) answer a motivated infinite-family problem; the distinct open-vs-closed chain spectral mechanisms offer a reusable computational structure.
